>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
In Jackson, Mississippi,
supporters of Scott Colombe are celebrating.
>> Mississippi Tech, Mississippi Tech, Mississippi Tech!
>> Supporters gathered at Tougaloo College in Jackson
to hear Colombe's victory speech
after the Associated Press called the race in Colombe's favor.
>> Colombe narrowly defeated Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde Smith
and now is set to become the first black Mississippi senator since Reconstruction.
He's also the first Democrat to win a Mississippi Senate seat since 1982.
But with a margin of victory of just a few thousand votes,
Elise Katrina Gregg of the Gulf States Newsroom
and Mississippi Public Broadcasting says there could be a legal challenge.
>> We do know that before this was all called,
the state GOP said that they would be looking at the legal options,
possible litigation, and just really closely monitoring the ballot count.
And to be clear, both candidates have had volunteers and lawyers monitoring the count.
We're likely to see some legal action come out of this at some point or another.
>> Colombe's victory expands the majority Senate Democrats will have
when the new Congress meets in January.
Alaska, now the only state where a Senate race remains undecided.
At least two people were killed, more than a dozen injured,
when a building collapsed in New York City late Wednesday afternoon.
Reporter Steve Kastenbaum says some survivors are in critical condition.
>> After the dust settled,
what was left standing in Brooklyn's Flappush neighborhood looked like it had been sliced open.
A staircase was exposed along with a bedroom and
a closet filled with clothing still on hangers.
Fire Department Chief John Esposito said rescue workers had to be very careful
as they searched for survivors in the rubble.
>> This is an extremely dangerous operation for all of our people.
>> Buildings Department Commissioner Ahmed Tigani said the structure collapsed into a construction site next door.
>> The type of work they were conducting was excavation work on that job site.
>> Some of those trapped were children.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Kastenbaum in Brooklyn, New York.
>> Peace talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have ended without a breakthrough.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports President Trump's envoys will next meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Head US negotiator and President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner told the media they had seen some openings and opportunities.
But few in Ukraine believe a window for serious diplomacy has opened.
Skeptical Ukrainian negotiators were instructed to approach the talks with an open mind if only to avoid annoying President Trump.
Ukrainians do not believe the Kremlin will miss the opportunity to pummel Ukraine's severely weakened energy infrastructure in this fifth winter of the war.
Analysts say Trump is looking for a foreign policy win after his midterm drubbing.
But Putin has not backed off any of his maximalist demands, such as Kiev handing over territory Russia has been unable to conquer.
Eleanor Beardsley in PR News, Kiev.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
Israel has attacked a hospital in southern Gaza, Gaza's health ministry.
Says Israel's airstrike on the Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunus killed six people and wounded at least a dozen more.
Israeli military says a senior Hamas member and other members of the group's armed wing were the strike's target,
claiming they were operating inside the hospital.
The Ebola case counts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, now over 11,000 people amid violence against treatment centers.
Here's NPR's Jonathan Lambert reporting.
About half of those 11,000 people who got Ebola have died, making this the deadliest outbreak in DRC's history.
Violence in parts of the country has disrupted the outbreak response.
Just last week, militants affiliated with the Islamic State burned down a treatment center near Breni,
killing nearly 50 people, according to health officials.
Given the rampant spread, the humanitarian organization MSF is urging the World Health Organization to approve wider use of Ervibo.
It's a vaccine licensed for another species of Ebola, but not the one behind this outbreak.
Clinical trials are ongoing, but results are many weeks away.
There has been some good news.
The last of nine Ebola patients in Kenya was discharged this week,
starting the 42-day countdown to certify that the country is Ebola-free.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
The troubles faced by key chipmaker NVIDIA weighing on global financial markets.
Asian chairs losing ground in Thursday trading amid reports that NVIDIA's board is meeting
to discuss the situation facing CEO Jensen Huang.
Huang's acknowledgment of an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has raised national security concerns.
